item.title: TYSON ON PROPERTY TAX RELIEF
item.description: Senate and house leaders, including the tax committee chairmen, met to lay the groundwork and coordinate moving on property tax reform. Senator Caryn Tyson says two key initiatives were discussed: the cap assessment protection amendment, SCR 1616, and a revenue cap proposal that would limit increases to no more than 3% without a vote of the people. item.title: ANCO TAX SALE
item.description: Anderson County’s latest round of sales of delinquent properties is set for March 30th. Twenty-two separate chunks of land are headed to the auction block. Under court order, the sheriff’s department is directed to advertise and sell the affected properties according to Kansas law. Proceeds from any sale will be applied to court and sales cost then outstanding tax liens. Several properties originally scheduled for auction have been reconciled. item.title: PAOLA LIBRARY GETS GRANT
item.description: Humanities Kansas recently awarded $1,804 to the Paola Free Library to support “Paola: A 1903 Snapshot,” a photograph digitization project to document and preserve the history of Paola. Paola Free Library Director, Morgan Menefee is serving as the project director. She says the project will preserve the story of Paola’s boom, including photos and information about many of the people responsible for Paola’s growth. item.title: Shannon Joseph Woolsey
item.description: Shannon Joseph Woolsey, 78, passed away peacefully Feb 5, 2026, at the Good Samaritan Nursing Home in Olathe, KS Shannon was the oldest son of Dale and Katherine Woolsey. He was born Feb 1,1948 in Garnet, KS. Because of his special needs, he attended Parsons State Hospital and Training Center in Parsons, KS from age 8 until 21. He worked with farm animals, in the automotive shop, and in the greenhouse. He enjoyed coming home for holidays and summer vacation.
